messages:
infra-alert-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: inference-frontend error rate spike in us-east-1c. 5xx rate > 12% for 3m. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/inf/err-rate?orgId=1&var-region=us-east-1c
ashok: seeing it too. routing latency + tail p95 up 300ms. any pager?
maria: @ashok I'm on it. starting with host health and ENI checks for us-east-1c pool.
netops-jen: AWS metric note: ENI attach/reassign errors reported in us-east-1c around 13:02 UTC. filing AWS SR now.
reggie-oncall: i'm taking P1. setting incident: P1 - us-east-1c network degradation affecting inference. paging oncall rota. (triggering runbook: infra->network->routing-fallback)
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-216. Runbook step 1: confirm scope, step 2: fail traffic to healthy zones, step 3: customer impact comms.
maria: quick diag: ssh to inference-node-ue1c-022 shows large dropped packets on eth0, kernel tx queue full. `ss -s` shows retransmits. grabbing dmesg.
maria: dmesg snippet:
```
[13:02:41] mlx5_core 0000:00:03.1: NIC link flapping, rps reset
[13:03:02] eth0: tx timeout, resetting
```
ashok: AWS console for the ASG shows a bunch of impaired instances in us-east-1c, health checks failing. ASG not replacing fast enough due to ENI allocation errors.
netops-jen: AWS SR says they're investigating a control plane ENI attach throttling impacting the AZ. ETA unknown. Suggest we stop creating more ENIs in the AZ and shift traffic out.
reggie-oncall: action list: 1) set smart-routing policy to prefer us-east-1a/1b, 2) start draining us-east-1c inference nodes, 3) bump cross-region capacity, 4) notify customers. I'm executing 1 now.
ashok: running control plane command to change route policy: `POST /v1/routing/policy` payload to increase weight on us-east-1a,b and reduce weight on us-east-1c.
maria: started node drain on ue1c pool: `./admin/drain_pool --pool ue1c-inference --grace 30s`
eng-sre: note: draining will spike latency for stateful KV cache misses. enable temporary KV warm cache in us-east-1a. Maria please trigger kvcache prewarm job.
maria: kicked off kvcache prewarm with job id prewarm-74321. monitor token cache fill.
ashok: also toggling model-fallback: downgrade default model for best-effort tier to smaller quantized variant to reduce GPU memory pressure while we move traffic. This is live for non-SLA customers only.
liza-cust-suc: customers seeing 502s? we have some reports from a few enterprise tenants. need a short customer message to post.
product-amy: priority: inform impacted customers with estimated mitigation steps and ETA, highlight that dedicated customers on reserved capacity in other AZs unaffected.
reggie-oncall: draft to customers (short):
```
Hi — we detected increased errors and latency for some inference requests in us-east-1c starting ~13:02 UTC. Our team is actively failing traffic to healthy zones (us-east-1a/1b) and draining unhealthy nodes. You may see elevated latency or transient 5xx for a small portion of requests for the next ~30–60m. We'll update when traffic is fully shifted. Contact support if you see persistent failures. — Redwood Inference
```
liza-cust-suc: sending now to impacted accounts and support channels.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: on-call escalation sent to @reggie-oncall, @maria, @ashok.
netops-jen: AWS suggests a temporary mitigation: avoid ENI churn by reusing existing warm instances in other AZs. They can't give ETA on control plane fix.
eng-sre: monitoring: error rate dropped to 4% after routing change, but latency p95 still +120ms relative to baseline. user-visible errors mostly from non-reserved traffic.
maria: health checks now show 90% of requests landing in us-east-1a/1b. finishing draining, will leave a small buffer capacity in ue1c for in-flight requests before scaling down.
ashok: rollback plan if cross-AZ shift fails: enable CDN-like response caching for inference-v2 small models (~5m expiry) to reduce backend load.
product-amy: any specfic customer SLAs impacted? Liza, please mark which tenants hit 5xx rates > threshold.
liza-cust-suc: marked 4 customers as impacted (enterprise ids E-224, E-330, E-411, E-905). support notified, ticket created per customer.
reggie-oncall: timeline so far: 13:02 detect -> 13:06 P1 declared -> 13:09 routing change -> 13:15 drain started -> 13:26 error rate stabilized ~4% -> 13:30 customer comms sent. assigning postmortem owner: @ashok.
ashok: will take postmortem. immediate blameless notes: AWS ENI attach/control plane degradation in us-east-1c caused ASG replacement churn and host-level NIC flapping. Our mitigation effective: smart-routing + drain + model-fallback.
incident-bot: Postmortem ticket created: PM-20260315-ue1c-network. Owner: ashok. Due date: 2026-03-22.
eng-sre: follow-ups: 1) improve smart-routing fast-fail thresholds, 2) add pre-warm cross-AZ instance pool capacity for heavy tail events, 3) add circuit breaker to block rapid ASG churn if ENI errors detected.
netops-jen: AWS SR updated: they acknowledge a control-plane ENI rate limit spike affecting allocations in us-east-1c. Will update when mitigated.
maria: wrapping up oncall handover to nightshift. leaving runbook notes and current state in incident doc.
reggie-oncall: handing to next oncall @maria for monitoring and postmortem prep. thanks everyone for quick triage. :thumbsup:
product-amy: will prepare customer-facing post-incident summary after postmortem.
ashok: lowering P1 to P2 at 13:47 UTC after stabilization and when AWS confirms reduced ENI errors. will re-open if regressions.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-216 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
